# Group-aware policy

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:identity-policy` · **Epic:** [#59](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/59) · **Tickets:** 14 (9S 5M)

Allow entries and MCP tool `allowWhen` conditions can be limited to IdP groups or specific users with `groups: [...]` / `users: [...]`. Entries without these fields behave exactly as today. A scoped entry never allows a request without a valid verified identity, a non-member is denied outright and never sent to the judge, and workers on older releases deny scoped destinations instead of allowing them. `warden policy eval` replay shows which users a candidate change affects.

## How we build it

- Schema: `config.AllowlistEntry` gains `Groups []string` and `Users []string` (yaml/json omitempty), and `config.MCPToolCondition` and `rawMCPToolCondition` gain `Groups`/`Users` next to `AgentID`/`TimeWindow`. Validation trims, rejects empty values, deduplicates and sorts, and caps each list at 256 values of 256 bytes. A Users value containing '@' is an email and is lowercased; any other value is an exact `sub`. Groups are exact, case-sensitive literals. The denylist and task-scope (`mcp.scopes.list[].constraints`) allowWhen get no scoping in P1. Entries without the fields marshal byte-identically to today, so existing ETags do not change. Old binaries reading a new local YAML fail at startup (KnownFields(true)), which fails closed.
- Merge safety: until enforcement lands, validation rejects non-empty Groups/Users with `not yet enforced`. W-P1-GPOL-10 lifts the guard for allow entries and W-P1-GPOL-11 for MCP tool conditions, and both depend on the fail-closed wire (W-P1-GPOL-06), so main never parses a scoped rule that some worker would treat as global.
- Fail-closed wire (W-P1-GPOL-06): the CP keeps serving one shared, ETag-versioned body. When building `policyWire` it moves allow entries that have groups/users out of `allowlist` into a new `scopedAllowlist` field, and for MCP tools with a scoped allowWhen it puts the real condition in a new wire-only `AllowWhenScoped` field and sets the legacy `AllowWhen` to a reserved AgentID sentinel `!identity-scoped` (rejected by validation as a real agent id). New workers merge both back in `parseRemotePolicy`. Old workers ignore the unknown fields, so scoped destinations stay NoMatch (denied) and scoped tools fail the sentinel condition (denied). The worker adds `grouppolicy/v1` to the heartbeat `caps` list (the caps struct and its CP-side registry are W-P1-BLOCK-10) for visibility only, and the fleet view flags workers without it while scoped rules exist (W-P1-GPOL-07).
- Subject: one type, `identity.Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, GroupsTruncated, AgentID}`, defined with `SubjectFrom` and `Claims.EmailVerified`/`Claims.GroupsTruncated` in the leaf package `internal/identity` by W-P1-VRFY-01, used by internal/policy, internal/mcp/gateway and internal/policyeval. `identity.SubjectFrom(claims, status)` returns nil unless the identity status is valid, so missing, invalid and expired tokens give a nil subject. A `users` email entry matches only when EmailVerified is true; `sub` entries always match exactly. One shared matcher, `identity.CompilePrincipals(...).Match(subject)` (W-P1-GPOL-02), is used by the evaluator and the MCP gateway. P2 worker-bound and P3 per-user-limits extend this type rather than redefine it.
- Evaluator (W-P1-GPOL-02): `Evaluate(domain, port, scheme)` stays destination-only and `EvaluateRequest(..., method, path)` stays the #371 per-request form returning a `RequestVerdict`. `EvaluateFor(RequestContext{Domain, Port, Scheme, Method, Path, Subject})` and the non-charging `PeekFor` evaluate a full request context and return a RequestVerdict-compatible result (`Decision`, `Reason`, `Scoped`); the method/path constraints of #371 apply per entry after the principal check. A new `Conditional` decision means a verified identity is required; it is never judge-eligible (a destination that matched any entry never returns NoMatch). `Evaluate` and `EvaluateRequest` collapse Conditional to Deny (`identity_required`) so every existing caller keeps default-deny. `load()` precompiles per-entry principal sets and a `hasScoped` flag, so policies without scoped entries keep the current allocation profile (asserted with testing.AllocsPerRun). Per entry the order is port and domain, then principal, then time window, method, path and rate limit, so non-members never consume a scoped entry's budget. Truncated groups: a member found in the (partial) list is allowed; a non-member of a truncated list is denied with the distinct reason `identity_groups_truncated`, never a silent plain deny; users-scoped entries are unaffected. A nil subject gives Conditional (`identity_required`); a non-member gives Deny (`group_not_allowed`). The denylist is still checked first. Rate-limit counters for scoped entries are keyed per entry index plus pattern:port; unscoped keys are unchanged. The three reasons are declared in `internal/denyreason`. Per-user limits come in P3.
- CONNECT and connection paths (W-P1-GPOL-03): the `needsJudge bool` threaded through handleConn, handleTLS, terminateAndDispatch, handleHTTP, serveHTTPRequest, handleGRPC and serveGRPCStream, and through the transparent listeners (#376: the :443 SNI path and the :80 plain-HTTP path, which have no CONNECT and no Proxy-Authorization), becomes a `deferred` enum {none, judge, identity}. The CONNECT gate switches exhaustively on the decision, with default meaning deny. Conditional without a CA gives 403 `identity_required`; with a CA (and on both transparent listeners) it proceeds with deferred=identity. A scoped Allow using the Proxy-Authorization subject proceeds likewise; without a CA the raw tunnel is closed at the token's `exp`. Non-TLS bytes and unknown protocols inside TLS fail closed when deferred != none. h2/gRPC streams run the shared request stages (handleGRPC -> serveGRPCStream -> runRequestStages) and are therefore decided per stream with that stream's subject.
- Request path (W-P1-GPOL-10): the per-request policy stage that already exists on main (`constraintGate`, which evaluates #371 constraints and counts the rate limit once per request on HTTP/1.1, WebSocket and every h2/gRPC stream) is extended, not duplicated, to call `EvaluateFor` with the request subject. It runs after `identityStage` (and the user block check) and before `judgeGate`. Keep-alive requests from different users and mid-session policy swaps are each decided correctly. Deny writes 403 with Event.Reason `identity_required`, `group_not_allowed` or `identity_groups_truncated` plus the VRFY user fields, and a scoped destination never reaches the judge.
- MCP (W-P1-GPOL-04, W-P1-GPOL-11): `OnRequest` gains a trailing `gateway.RequestMeta{Subject *identity.Subject}` parameter on proxy.MCPGateway (proxy.go), proxy.WSScanner (proxy.go) and the ws.Pump gateway interface (internal/mcp/ws/pump.go), and on all callers and fakes (GPOL-04, no behaviour change). http.go passes the request subject; ws.Pump stores the subject verified on the upgrade request; the stdio pump passes nil, so group-gated tools are denied over stdio. `compileConditions` adds the shared principal matcher and `conditionDenies` fails with the existing Kind `mcp_tool_condition` and Detail `no verified identity`, `user not permitted` or (truncated list, not found) `groups truncated`, whose Verdict.Reason is `identity_groups_truncated` (GPOL-11). P1 gates whole tools only; per-group argument constraints come later. The session key (`agentID:domain`) is unchanged in P1.
- Replay and lint: `policyeval.Evaluate` builds a subject from Event.UserSub/UserEmail/UserGroups only when the recorded identity status is valid, calls EvaluateFor with the recorded method and path, and maps Conditional to deny. EvalDiff gains `AffectedUsers` (up to 20, sorted), `AffectedUsersTotal` and `AnonymousCount`. `warden policy eval` prints them and accepts `--user` (W-P1-GPOL-05). A new `config.LintScoped` warns about scoped entries shadowed by an unscoped or wildcard entry for the same destination and `warden policy eval` prints the warnings (W-P1-GPOL-12). Workers log once per agent when scoped entries exist but that agent's identity mode is off.
- Observability: scoped denies go through emitDeny, so `RecordBlocked("identity_required"|"group_not_allowed"|"identity_groups_truncated")` receives the declared reasons from `internal/denyreason`; a new OTel counter `warden.policy.scoped.total{result=allow|not_member|no_identity}` (Prometheus name warden_policy_scoped_total) has no user or group labels. Raw tokens, group lists and emails never appear in metric labels or debug logs. The decision-log reason enum is derived from denyreason.Declared() by W-P1-JAUD-02.
- Dashboard (W-P1-GPOL-08): the CP policy editor adds groups/users chip inputs per allow entry and per MCP allowWhen, saved through `/dashboard/api/policy` and the existing policy writer; the worker and CP policy views show a `scoped` badge and the lint warnings. Sorted, normalized groups/users keep ETags and the P1 policy-history diff deterministic.
- Tests and docs: W-P1-GPOL-09 holds the L1 scenarios (test/scenarios on the test/harness in-process rig with the VRFY-05 issuer fake), W-P1-GPOL-14 repeats the core cases once against real Dex on the L2 stack (W-P1-DEX-04), and W-P1-GPOL-13 documents the feature in docs/group-policy.md.

## Done when

On a CA-enabled worker in attribute mode with `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}` and no unscoped entry for that host: a valid Dex token for an eng member is allowed over both Proxy-Authorization and X-Warden-Identity; a non-member gets 403 `group_not_allowed`; anonymous, invalid and expired tokens get 403 `identity_required`; a token whose groups list was truncated is allowed when the group is in the partial list and denied with `identity_groups_truncated` otherwise; within one keep-alive session (and across h2 streams) requests from different users are each decided correctly; a Conditional CONNECT with no CA, or one that switches to non-TLS bytes or an unknown protocol, is denied and the judge is never consulted. An MCP tool with `allowWhen.groups: [finance]` is denied to eng and allowed to finance in enforce mode. A worker on the previous release that receives this policy from the CP denies api.github.com and the gated tool, and the fleet view flags it. `warden policy eval` against a candidate that removes eng access lists only the affected eng users plus a count of anonymous events. Deny events, decision logs and metrics carry the three new reasons.

### 1/14 · W-P1-GPOL-01

**Add groups/users to allow entries and MCP conditions schema**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#60](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/60)

**Context.** Group-aware policy lets an allow entry or an MCP tool `allowWhen` be limited to IdP groups or named users. The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (GitHub #60) is the config-only foundation: it adds the fields, normalization, deep copies and a fail-closed validation guard. Until the evaluator and gateway enforce the fields, any config that sets them is rejected, so main never parses a scoped rule that would be treated as global. W-P1-GPOL-10 lifts the guard for allow entries and W-P1-GPOL-11 for MCP conditions, both only after the fail-closed wire (W-P1-GPOL-06) exists.

OUT of scope: evaluation (W-P1-GPOL-02), the old-worker wire handling (W-P1-GPOL-06), the shadow lint (W-P1-GPOL-12).

**What to build.** Config fields, `normalizePrincipals`, the guard, deep copies and tests in `internal/config`.

**Requirements**

- `config.AllowlistEntry` (internal/config/config.go) gains `Groups []string` and `Users []string` (yaml `groups,omitempty` / `users,omitempty`, json the same); `MCPToolCondition` and `rawMCPToolCondition` (internal/config/mcp.go) gain the same fields next to `AgentID`/`TimeWindow`, populated in the raw-to-typed conversion.
- Normalization in a new `normalizePrincipals(path string, groups, users []string) ([]string, []string, error)`: trim each value, reject empty strings, deduplicate and sort, cap each list at 256 values of at most 256 bytes. A Users value containing `@` is an email and is lowercased; any other Users value is an exact `sub`. Groups are exact, case-sensitive literals. Errors name the field path (for example `policy.allowlist[2].groups[1]`).
- Guard: `validate(p Policy)` (config.go) and `validateMCPConstraints` (mcp.go) reject any non-empty Groups/Users on an allow entry or an MCP tool `allowWhen` with an error naming the field path and `not yet enforced`. W-P1-GPOL-10 and W-P1-GPOL-11 lift it per path.
- Scoped fields stay rejected permanently in P1 on denylist entries (strict `KnownFields`, no field exists) and in task-scope `mcp.scopes.list[].constraints` allowWhen. The denylist is global.
- The AgentID value `!identity-scoped` is reserved for the wire sentinel of W-P1-GPOL-06 and is rejected in any allowWhen as an agent id.
- `Policy.DeepCopy` (config.go), `cloneToolConstraints` (mcp.go) and `copyToolConstraints` (settings.go) clone the Groups/Users slices so copies never alias.
- Entries without the fields marshal byte-identically to today in YAML and JSON (`omitempty`), so existing ETags do not change.
- Old binaries reading a new local YAML fail at startup (`KnownFields(true)`), which fails closed.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/config.
2. internal/config/config.go: add the fields to AllowlistEntry; deep-copy them in Policy.DeepCopy.
3. internal/config/mcp.go: add the fields to MCPToolCondition and rawMCPToolCondition; copy them in the raw conversion and in cloneToolConstraints.
4. internal/config/settings.go: deep-copy Groups/Users in copyToolConstraints.
5. New normalizePrincipals called from validate and validateMCPConstraints, followed by the temporary guard error and the sentinel check.
6. configs/config.example.yaml: add commented examples under policy.allowlist and an mcp.tools.constraints allowWhen (marked as not yet enforced).
7. Run `go test ./internal/config`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given `groups: [' eng ', eng]` and `users: [Alice@Corp.Example, 'u-123']`, the normalizer returns Groups==[eng] and Users==[alice@corp.example, u-123]; an empty value, a 257-value list and a 257-byte value each fail with the field path: `go test ./internal/config -run TestNormalizePrincipals`. Red first: fails to compile before the function exists.
- [ ] Any allow entry or MCP allowWhen with non-empty groups or users fails to load with an error containing the field path and `not yet enforced`: `go test ./internal/config -run 'TestAllowlistGroupsRejectedUntilEnforced|TestMCPAllowWhenGroupsRejectedUntilEnforced'`.
- [ ] `groups` on a denylist entry, and groups in a task-scope allowWhen, fail to load: `go test ./internal/config -run 'TestDenylistGroupsRejected|TestScopeConstraintGroupsRejected'`.
- [ ] An allowWhen with `agentID: '!identity-scoped'` fails to load: `go test ./internal/config -run TestReservedScopedSentinelRejected`.
- [ ] A DeepCopy of a policy with Groups/Users does not alias: mutating the copy's Groups[0] leaves the original unchanged (also for the MCP constraint copies): `go test ./internal/config -run TestDeepCopy_GroupsNotAliased`.
- [ ] A policy without the fields marshals to the same YAML and JSON bytes as a pre-change golden: `go test ./internal/config -run TestUnscopedPolicyMarshalUnchanged`.
- [ ] Existing config tests pass unchanged. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-APPR-02`](policy-approvals.md#29--w-p2-appr-02) Implement widening-change classification; [`W-P1-GPOL-06`](identity-policy.md#214--w-p1-gpol-06) Project scoped rules into fail-closed policy wire fields; [`W-P1-GPOL-02`](identity-policy.md#314--w-p1-gpol-02) Make the policy evaluator subject-aware: EvaluateFor and PeekFor with a request context; [`W-P1-GPOL-12`](identity-policy.md#914--w-p1-gpol-12) Add config.LintScoped shadow warnings and print them in policy eval; [`W-P3-PUL-01`](per-user-limits.md#110--w-p3-pul-01) Add userLimits config, costBlockedUsers wire type and validation

### 2/14 · W-P1-GPOL-06

**Project scoped rules into fail-closed policy wire fields**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#244](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/244)

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-06, GitHub #244) makes the CP-to-worker wire safe for workers that do not understand scoped rules. Old workers decode the CP policy with lenient JSON, so they would drop `groups` and treat a scoped entry as global. The CP keeps serving one shared, ETag-versioned body but moves scoped allow entries into a new `scopedAllowlist` field and replaces a scoped MCP `allowWhen` with a reserved sentinel, so old workers deny and new workers merge the real rules back. It must land before W-P1-GPOL-10 and W-P1-GPOL-11 lift the config guard, so main never serves a scoped rule that a worker could read as global.

OUT of scope: enforcement (W-P1-GPOL-10/-11); the heartbeat capability and fleet badge (W-P1-GPOL-07). Versioned policy mode (W-P1-PVER-01) serves through the same single wire build, so the projection lives at that one place and needs no ordering with PVER.

**What to build.** Wire fields and the projection in `internal/controlplane` and the merge in `internal/config/remote.go`.

**Requirements**

- `policyWire` (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) gains `ScopedAllowlist []config.AllowlistEntry` json `scopedAllowlist,omitempty`; allow entries with groups/users are moved there and left out of `allowlist`, keeping relative order.
- For MCP tools whose `allowWhen` has groups/users, the wire carries the real condition in a new wire-only field `AllowWhenScoped` on `MCPToolConstraints` (`yaml:"-"`, json-encoded in the wire) and sets the legacy `AllowWhen` to `{AgentID: "!identity-scoped"}`. A pre-change gateway therefore fails the sentinel condition and denies the tool.
- A new `projectScoped(p config.Policy, s *config.SettingsWire)` is called in the one place the wire is built (`internal/controlplane/policyserver.go`, for file mode and versioned mode alike).
- `parseRemotePolicy` and the SettingsWire apply step in `internal/config/remote.go` (`remoteWire`) merge `scopedAllowlist` and `AllowWhenScoped` back deterministically (scoped entries re-inserted in their original order) and fail the pull if a sentinel remains without a scoped condition, so the worker keeps its last good policy.
- Policies without scoped rules produce byte-identical wire JSON and the same ETag as before.
- Serving stays one body per ETag; no per-worker policy bodies.

**Implementation plan**

1. Record the wire JSON and ETag of an unscoped fixture policy on main as a golden before editing.
2. Write the failing tests first in internal/controlplane and internal/config.
3. internal/config/mcp.go: add AllowWhenScoped and copy it in the clone helpers.
4. internal/controlplane: add ScopedAllowlist to policyWire and projectScoped, called from the wire build.
5. internal/config/remote.go: extend remoteWire and merge in parseRemotePolicy and the settings apply step; reject a dangling sentinel.
6. Run `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/config`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An unscoped policy serves the same body and ETag as the pre-change golden: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyWire_UnscopedUnchanged`.
- [ ] A scoped entry is absent from `allowlist` and present in `scopedAllowlist`, and a new worker's parsed Policy contains it with Groups set and the original order: `go test ./internal/config -run TestParseRemotePolicy_Scoped`. Red first: fails before the field exists.
- [ ] A scoped MCP tool is projected with the sentinel and `AllowWhenScoped`, and the new worker restores the real condition: `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/config -run 'TestProjectScoped_MCP|TestParseRemotePolicy_ScopedMCP'`.
- [ ] Decoding the wire with the previous `remoteWire` shape (a frozen test copy) yields no allow entry for the scoped host (NoMatch -> denied) and an allowWhen that the current gateway denies: `go test ./internal/config -run TestOldWorkerDeniesScoped`.
- [ ] A pull whose settings contain the sentinel without AllowWhenScoped fails with an error and the worker keeps its last good policy: `go test ./internal/config -run TestParseRemotePolicy_DanglingSentinel`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 3/14 · W-P1-GPOL-02

**Make the policy evaluator subject-aware: EvaluateFor and PeekFor with a request context**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#61](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/61)

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-02, GitHub #61) is the policy-package core: it teaches `internal/policy` to decide a request for a subject. On main, `Evaluate(domain, port, scheme)` is destination-only and `EvaluateRequest(domain, port, scheme, method, path)` returns a `RequestVerdict` with the #371 method/path constraints; this ticket adds `EvaluateFor`/`PeekFor`, which take the full request context and return a RequestVerdict-compatible result, plus a new `Conditional` decision. `Conditional` means a destination is only reachable with a verified identity; it is never judge-eligible and callers that do not know it must treat it as deny.

Merging changes no behaviour: the guard from W-P1-GPOL-01 still rejects scoped rules, so only tests build scoped evaluators. W-P1-GPOL-03 and W-P1-GPOL-10 use these functions in the proxy; W-P1-GPOL-05 uses them in replay; W-P1-GPOL-11 reuses the principal matcher added here.

OUT of scope: any change to `internal/proxy` behaviour (W-P1-GPOL-03/-10), MCP conditions (W-P1-GPOL-11), per-user limits (P3).

**What to build.** Types and the evaluator walk in `internal/policy/policy.go`, three new reason constants in `internal/denyreason`, and a shared principal matcher in `internal/identity`.

**Requirements**

- In `internal/policy/policy.go` add `type RequestContext struct{Domain string; Port int; Scheme Scheme; Method, Path string; Subject *identity.Subject}`. `Method == ""` means the CONNECT / destination-only form (constraints could-match, rate limit peeked) exactly as `EvaluateRequest(..., "", "")` today; a non-empty method means per-request enforcement (constraints enforced, rate limit counted).
- `func (e *Evaluator) EvaluateFor(rc RequestContext) RequestVerdict` and `func (e *Evaluator) PeekFor(rc RequestContext) RequestVerdict`. PeekFor runs the same walk but never charges a rate-limit counter in any mode (used by explain tooling in P4 and available to callers that decide before charging). `RequestVerdict` gains `Scoped bool`, true when at least one scoped entry matched the destination, so the decision depends on identity.
- New `Decision` value `Conditional` appended after `NoMatch` (existing numeric values unchanged), `String()` returns `conditional`. It is never judge-eligible by construction.
- Compatibility: `EvaluateRequest` becomes `EvaluateFor` with a nil Subject and collapses a `Conditional` result to `RequestVerdict{Decision: Deny, Reason: identity_required}`; `Evaluate` keeps its signature and returns only Allow, Deny or NoMatch (Conditional collapses to Deny). Every existing caller therefore stays default-deny for scoped destinations.
- Reasons: declare `IdentityRequired = "identity_required"`, `GroupNotAllowed = "group_not_allowed"` and `IdentityGroupsTruncated = "identity_groups_truncated"` in `internal/denyreason/reasons.go`, add them to the `declared` list and keep `TestDeclaredSetIsWellFormed`, `TestRequiredReasonsDeclared` and `TestNoReasonLiteralsOutsideTheDeclaredSet` green. No other file may spell the values.
- Subject: use `identity.Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID, GroupsTruncated}` and `SubjectFrom(claims, status)` from W-P1-VRFY-01; never define a second Subject. The subject must carry `GroupsTruncated`, copied from `Claims.GroupsTruncated` by `SubjectFrom`; if the merged W-P1-VRFY-01 does not have the field, add the field and the copy here with `TestSubjectFromCopiesGroupsTruncated` in internal/identity.
- Shared matcher in a new `internal/identity/principals.go`: `CompilePrincipals(groups, users []string) Principals` and `(Principals) Match(s *Subject) MatchResult` with results `NoIdentity` (nil subject), `Member`, `NotMember`, `TruncatedMiss` (not a member while `GroupsTruncated` is set and no user entry matched). A `users` entry containing `@` matches only when `Subject.Email` equals it and `Subject.EmailVerified` is true; any other `users` entry matches `Subject.Sub` exactly; `groups` entries match any element of `Subject.Groups` exactly (case-sensitive). An entry with both lists matches when either does. A member found in a truncated list is a member. W-P1-GPOL-11 reuses this type.
- Per-entry order inside the evaluator: port and domain, then principal, then time window, then method, then path, then rate limit, so a non-member never consumes a scoped entry's rate budget and a method/path constraint is only judged for a principal the entry admits. Unscoped entries admit everyone (including a nil subject). The denylist is still checked first and the canonical-path pre-pass is unchanged.
- Outcome rules: Allow if any entry admits the request. Otherwise, if a scoped entry was skipped because the subject is nil: `Conditional` with reason `identity_required` (this takes precedence over other rejections because identity could still satisfy the entry). Otherwise if a principal-admitted entry was rejected by a guard: the existing reason (path_not_allowed, method_not_allowed, time_window, rate_limited). Otherwise, for scoped entries only: `Deny` with `identity_groups_truncated` when any scoped entry produced `TruncatedMiss`, else `Deny` with `group_not_allowed`. A destination that matched any entry by domain and port never returns NoMatch, so it can never reach the judge. Users-only entries are unaffected by truncation.
- Rate-limit counters for scoped entries are keyed by entry index plus pattern:port (today the key is the pattern:port shared across entries); unscoped keys are unchanged. The counters reset on `Replace` exactly as today (per-user limit buckets that survive Replace are W-P3-PUL-03).
- `load()` precompiles one `Principals` per scoped entry and a `hasScoped` flag under `swapMu`. With no scoped entries `EvaluateFor` with a nil subject takes the current path and allocates exactly as `EvaluateRequest` does on main.

**Implementation plan**

1. Measure `testing.AllocsPerRun` of `EvaluateRequest` on an unscoped 50-entry policy on main before editing and record the number in the test as the baseline.
2. Write the failing tests first: internal/policy/policy_scoped_test.go, internal/identity/principals_test.go, denyreason tests.
3. internal/denyreason/reasons.go: add the three constants and list them in declared.
4. internal/identity/principals.go: CompilePrincipals/Match (and Subject.GroupsTruncated if missing).
5. internal/policy/policy.go: RequestContext, Conditional, Scoped, load() precompilation, the shared walk, EvaluateFor/PeekFor and the compatibility wrappers.
6. Run `go test -race ./internal/policy ./internal/identity ./internal/denyreason ./internal/proxy`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}`, EvaluateFor gives Allow for a subject with groups [eng], Deny/`group_not_allowed` for [sales] and Conditional/`identity_required` for nil, and `Evaluate` gives Deny for nil: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_Scoped`. Red first: fails to compile before the types exist.
- [ ] Given `users: [alice@corp.example]`, a subject with that email and EmailVerified=false gets Deny, with EmailVerified=true gets Allow; a `users: [u-123]` entry matches Sub exactly: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_UsersAndVerifiedEmail`.
- [ ] Truncated groups: a subject with GroupsTruncated=true and groups [eng] is Allowed by an `eng` entry; with groups [sales] it is Denied with `identity_groups_truncated` (not `group_not_allowed`); a `users` entry that matches still Allows; a non-truncated non-member still gets `group_not_allowed`: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_TruncatedGroups`.
- [ ] Method/path constraints apply after the principal check: with `{domain: d, groups: [eng], methods: [GET]}`, an eng subject POSTing gets Deny/`method_not_allowed`, a sales subject POSTing gets `group_not_allowed`, nil gets Conditional: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_ConstraintsAfterPrincipal`.
- [ ] With a scoped entry and an unscoped entry for the same host, a nil subject is Allowed by the unscoped entry; a deny-listed host is Deny even for a member: `go test ./internal/policy -run 'TestEvaluateFor_MixedScopedUnscoped|TestEvaluateFor_DenylistWins'`.
- [ ] A scoped entry with `rateLimit: 1/minute` still allows a member after non-member and nil-subject calls, and scoped and unscoped entries for one host use different counters: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_ScopedRateBuckets`.
- [ ] `PeekFor` never charges: after N PeekFor calls the same budget is still available to EvaluateFor: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestPeekFor_NoCharge`.
- [ ] `Evaluate` never returns Conditional and `EvaluateRequest` on a scoped-only host with no subject returns Deny/`identity_required`: `go test ./internal/policy -run 'TestEvaluate_NeverConditional|TestEvaluateRequest_ScopedCollapsesToDeny'`.
- [ ] `testing.AllocsPerRun` of `EvaluateFor` with a nil subject on an unscoped policy equals the recorded `EvaluateRequest` baseline: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_NoScopedAllocs`.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_ConcurrentReplace` passes with Replace racing EvaluateFor/PeekFor.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run 'TestPrincipals|TestSubjectFromCopiesGroupsTruncated'` and `go test ./internal/denyreason` pass; existing `go test ./internal/policy ./internal/proxy` pass unchanged. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 4/14 · W-P1-GPOL-03

**Thread a deferred enum through CONNECT, TLS, HTTP, gRPC and the transparent listeners and fail closed on identity-conditional decisions**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#62](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/62)

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-03, GitHub #62) keeps the original key of the proxy-side ticket and is its foundation half: the connection-level handling of the new evaluator decisions. The original #62 was split in two because it combined a signature-wide refactor of six functions across four files with the new per-request stage, metrics and the removal of the config guard; the per-request half is W-P1-GPOL-10.

On main, whether a request still needs an LLM judge is threaded as a `needsJudge bool` through `handleConn`, `handleTLS`, `terminateAndDispatch`, `handleHTTP`, `serveHTTPRequest`, `handleGRPC` and `serveGRPCStream`, and on the transparent listeners (`internal/proxy/transparent.go`, #376). A scoped destination needs a second kind of deferral: the decision cannot be finished at CONNECT because it depends on the identity of each request. This ticket replaces the bool with a `deferred` enum everywhere and makes every connection-level path fail closed for the new `Conditional` and scoped decisions. Because `constraintGate` still evaluates with `EvaluateRequest` (nil subject), every request of a deferred-identity session is denied `identity_required` until W-P1-GPOL-10 passes the request subject; the config guard from W-P1-GPOL-01 additionally keeps scoped rules from loading, so main is safe at every step.

OUT of scope: the per-request decision with the subject, reasons on request events, metrics and lifting the guard (W-P1-GPOL-10); MCP (W-P1-GPOL-04/-11).

**What to build.** `internal/proxy/deferred.go` (new) and the signature changes and gate switches described below.

**Requirements**

- New `internal/proxy/deferred.go`: `type deferred uint8` with `deferNone`, `deferJudge`, `deferIdentity`, a `String()`, and `deferredFor(v policy.RequestVerdict) deferred` (NoMatch -> deferJudge; Conditional or a Scoped Allow -> deferIdentity; plain Allow -> deferNone). Decisions are mutually exclusive: a destination is either NoMatch or it matched an entry.
- Replace the `needsJudge bool` parameter and the `requestScope.needsJudge` field with `deferred` in `handleConn` (serve.go), `handleTLS` and `terminateAndDispatch` (tls.go), `handleHTTP`, `serveHTTPRequest` and `requestScope` (http.go), `handleGRPC` and `serveGRPCStream` (grpc.go), and in the transparent HTTPS path (`handleTransparentTLS`, which calls `terminateAndDispatch`) and the transparent plain-HTTP path (`handleTransparentHTTP`, which calls `handleHTTP`) in transparent.go. `judgeGate` runs when `s.deferred == deferJudge`; behaviour for `deferNone` and `deferJudge` is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- CONNECT gate: `handleConn` calls `p.cfg.Policy.EvaluateFor(policy.RequestContext{Domain, Port, Scheme: policy.SchemeHTTPS, Subject: <CONNECT subject>})` where the subject is the connection's verified subject from W-P1-VRFY-02 (`connIdentity`; non-nil only for status valid, so missing, invalid, expired and unverified tokens give nil). `Method` stays empty (destination-only admission). The tri-state `if` becomes an exhaustive `switch verdict.Decision` over Allow, NoMatch, Conditional and Deny whose `default` denies (reason `policy_no_match` with an ERROR log `unhandled policy decision`), so any future value fails closed. The same switch is used by the two transparent gates through one shared helper so the three gates cannot diverge.
- Conditional (no CONNECT subject): with a CA, send `200 Connection Established` and continue to TLS with `deferIdentity`; without a CA a raw tunnel cannot be re-checked per request, so respond `403`, store a deny event with reason `identity_required` and never dial. Transparent HTTPS (SNI) has no Proxy-Authorization, so it always continues with `deferIdentity`; transparent plain HTTP carries only `X-Warden-Identity`, so it continues into `handleHTTP` with `deferIdentity` (no CA is involved).
- Scoped Allow (member at CONNECT): with a CA continue with `deferIdentity` (each request is re-decided by W-P1-GPOL-10). Without a CA the raw tunnel is allowed but its connection deadline is set to the token's expiry (`connIdentity.Expiry`) so the tunnel is cut when the token expires; a zero expiry is treated as deny `identity_required`. A policy swap does not cut such a raw tunnel (documented limitation, W-P1-GPOL-13).
- Fail closed inside TLS: in `handleTLS` and `terminateAndDispatch` every branch that cannot run the per-request stages (non-TLS bytes after CONNECT, unknown protocol inside TLS) is denied whenever `deferred != deferNone`, with the reason the judge path already uses (`no_tls`), or `identity_required` when `deferred == deferIdentity`. HTTP/1.1, WebSocket upgrades and h2/gRPC streams all run `runRequestStages`, so they continue and are decided per request (h2 behaviour on main: `handleGRPC` -> `serveGRPCStream` -> `runRequestStages`).
- The judge is never consulted for a `deferIdentity` session by this ticket: `judgeGate` only runs for `deferJudge`.
- With no scoped entries and no Conditional result nothing observable changes: existing proxy, scenario and e2e tests pass with only helper signature updates.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/proxy (deferred_test.go, plus transparent_test.go additions).
2. New internal/proxy/deferred.go; change signatures in serve.go, tls.go, http.go, grpc.go, transparent.go and every test helper that calls them.
3. serve.go and transparent.go: shared gate helper with the exhaustive switch; CONNECT subject lookup from connIdentity (W-P1-VRFY-02); raw-tunnel expiry deadline.
4. tls.go: fail closed when deferred != deferNone on the non-HTTP branches.
5. Run `go test -race ./internal/proxy ./test/scenarios`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With an evaluator built directly from a policy that has `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}` (tests bypass the config guard) and a CA: a CONNECT with an eng token on Proxy-Authorization gets `200` and proceeds with `deferIdentity`; a CONNECT with no token also gets `200` and proceeds with `deferIdentity`; every HTTP request on either tunnel is answered 403 `identity_required` because the request-time subject arrives in W-P1-GPOL-10: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestDeferredIdentity_ConnectWithCA`. Red first: fails to compile before the enum exists.
- [ ] Without a CA, an anonymous CONNECT to a scoped-only host gets 403 and one deny event with reason `identity_required` and no upstream dial: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestDeferredIdentity_NoCA`.
- [ ] A scoped Allow without a CA is raw-tunneled and the connection is closed at the token expiry (fake clock/short expiry); a zero expiry is denied: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestDeferredIdentity_RawTunnelExpiry`.
- [ ] With a CA and a deferred-identity CONNECT, sending non-TLS bytes or negotiating an unknown protocol inside TLS closes the connection with no upstream dial and a deny event (`no_tls` / `identity_required`); with a judge fake that always allows, the fake gets zero calls: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestDeferredIdentity_FailClosedBranches`.
- [ ] The transparent :443 and :80 listeners continue with `deferIdentity` for a Conditional destination and deny a scoped-only destination on :443 when the ClientHello cannot be terminated: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestTransparent_DeferredIdentity`.
- [ ] An evaluator that returns an unknown Decision value makes the CONNECT gate deny with a declared reason and the ERROR log: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestConnectGate_UnknownDecisionFailsClosed`.
- [ ] `grep -rn needsJudge internal/proxy --include=*.go` finds no match outside comments, and existing tests pass: `go test -race ./internal/proxy ./test/scenarios`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-02`](identity-policy.md#314--w-p1-gpol-02) Make the policy evaluator subject-aware: EvaluateFor and PeekFor with a request context; [`W-P1-VRFY-02`](identity-verification.md#211--w-p1-vrfy-02) Extract and verify identity on CONNECT, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 before the proxy-only strip

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-GPOL-10`](identity-policy.md#514--w-p1-gpol-10) Decide scoped allow entries on every request with the request subject, add reasons and metrics and lift the allow-entry guard; [`W-P4-HOOK-07`](policy-hooks.md#711--w-p4-hook-07) Wire the pre-request hook stage into the HTTP/1.1 proxy path

### 5/14 · W-P1-GPOL-10

**Decide scoped allow entries on every request with the request subject, add reasons and metrics and lift the allow-entry guard**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue —

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-10) is the second half of the original proxy ticket #62 (the first half, W-P1-GPOL-03, holds the `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling). One keep-alive tunnel can carry requests from different users, so the decision has to be re-made per request with that request's subject, on HTTP/1.1, WebSocket upgrades and every h2/gRPC stream.

On main every request of every protocol already passes `constraintGate` in `runRequestStages` (internal/proxy/http.go), which evaluates the live policy with `EvaluateRequest` for the #371 method/path constraints and counts the rate limit exactly once. Adding a second evaluating stage would double-charge rate limits, so this ticket extends that stage to pass the request subject (the name `scopedPolicyStage` used in later-phase tickets refers to this stage's slot). The stage runs after `identityStage` (W-P1-VRFY-02) and, when present, the user block check (W-P1-BLOCK-02), and before `judgeGate`.

OUT of scope: the enum and CONNECT handling (W-P1-GPOL-03); MCP conditions (W-P1-GPOL-11); the fleet badge (W-P1-GPOL-07).

**What to build.** The stage change, deny reasons on events, the metric, the one-per-agent warning, and removal of the allow-entry part of the config guard.

**Requirements**

- Order of stages in `runRequestStages`: `readRequest`, `stripHopHeaders`, `identityStage` (W-P1-VRFY-02), the user block check when W-P1-BLOCK-02 has landed, then the policy stage, then `judgeGate`. If `constraintGate` currently precedes `identityStage`, move it after; the block stage inserts itself before the policy stage.
- The policy stage calls `p.cfg.Policy.EvaluateFor(policy.RequestContext{Domain, Port, Scheme, Method, Path: req.URL.EscapedPath(), Subject: s.subject})` where `s.subject` is the request's verified subject from W-P1-VRFY-02 (non-nil only for status valid; header identity wins when present, two different valid subjects give conflict and a nil subject). It is the only per-request policy evaluation (single charge). NoMatch falls through to the judge exactly as before; Allow continues; Deny and Conditional are terminal: `emitDeny` with the verdict's reason (`group_not_allowed`, `identity_groups_truncated`, `identity_required`, or the existing constraint reasons) and a 403. A scoped destination never reaches `judgeGate` or any later stage.
- The same stage serves h2/gRPC streams (`serveGRPCStream` runs `runRequestStages`), so the subject is decided per stream. A token that expires mid-session is re-checked on each request through the W-P1-VRFY-02 expiry rule, so an expired token gives nil and `identity_required`.
- Deny events and decision logs carry the new reasons plus the user fields that W-P1-VRFY-03 stamps through `recordEvent` (identity_status, user_sub); `RecordBlocked(reason)` already receives the reason from `emitDeny`. Raw tokens, emails and group lists never appear in events' reason, metric labels or logs.
- New OTel counter `warden.policy.scoped.total{result=allow|not_member|no_identity}` (Prometheus name `warden_policy_scoped_total`) in `internal/observability`, nil-safe, with no user or group labels, recorded by the stage when the verdict is Scoped: Allow -> `allow`, Deny group_not_allowed or identity_groups_truncated -> `not_member`, Conditional -> `no_identity`. Add the method to the proxy `MetricsRecorder` interface and every fake in the proxy tests.
- When scoped entries exist and an agent's identity mode is off, log one WARN per agent (and per scoped-entry count) from the worker where policy and identity settings are applied, with the count of scoped entries and never group names.
- Remove the allow-entry part of the W-P1-GPOL-01 validation guard in `internal/config` (MCP and denylist/scope paths stay rejected). This is safe only because W-P1-GPOL-06 already projects scoped entries into the fail-closed wire; this ticket therefore depends on it.
- With no scoped entries the stage, events and metrics are unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/proxy (group_policy_test.go) using the W-P1-VRFY fake verifier and a fake judge.
2. internal/proxy/http.go: pass the subject in the policy stage, map the verdict, reorder after identityStage.
3. internal/observability: add the counter and RecordScoped; update the MetricsRecorder interface and proxy test fakes.
4. internal/worker: add the identity-off warning on policy/identity apply.
5. internal/config: remove the allow-entry part of the guard; update configs/config.example.yaml comments.
6. Run `go test -race ./internal/proxy ./internal/config ./internal/observability ./internal/worker ./test/scenarios`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}` and a CA, an eng token on Proxy-Authorization is forwarded and a sales token gets 403 with a deny event reason `group_not_allowed`: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGroupPolicy_ConnectIdentity`. Red first: fails before the subject is passed.
- [ ] On one keep-alive tunnel with no Proxy-Authorization, an eng X-Warden-Identity request gets 200 and a following sales request gets 403, and an h2 tunnel decides each stream by its own subject: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestGroupPolicy_RequestIdentity|TestGroupPolicy_H2PerStream'`.
- [ ] Anonymous, invalid, expired and conflicting-identity requests to a scoped-only host are denied with `identity_required` and the event carries identity_status (for example `expired`): `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGroupPolicy_NoIdentityReasons`.
- [ ] With a judge fake that always allows, non-member and anonymous requests to a scoped-only host are denied and the fake gets zero calls: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGroupPolicy_NeverJudged`.
- [ ] A truncated-groups token hits both branches: a member found in the partial list is allowed, a non-member is denied with `identity_groups_truncated`: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGroupPolicy_TruncatedGroups`.
- [ ] A policy swap mid-session that removes a group is applied to the next request on the same tunnel: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGroupPolicy_PolicySwapMidSession`.
- [ ] A rate-limited scoped entry is charged once per request (not twice) and non-members do not consume it: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGroupPolicy_RateChargedOnce`.
- [ ] `warden_policy_scoped_total` increments with result `allow`, `not_member` and `no_identity` and has no user or group label, and no test output contains a raw token, email or group name in labels: `go test ./internal/proxy ./internal/observability -run 'Scoped'`.
- [ ] With scoped entries and identity mode off the worker logs exactly one WARN per agent: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestScopedEntriesIdentityOffWarns`.

**Pass the verified subject to the MCP gateway through RequestMeta**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#63](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/63)

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-04, GitHub #63) keeps the original key of the MCP ticket and is its plumbing half: it changes the `OnRequest` seam so the verified subject reaches the gateway on every transport, with no behaviour change. The original #63 was split because the group/user `allowWhen` logic (W-P1-GPOL-11) needs this seam but P4 tickets (W-P4-DGR-05, W-P4-MGW-13) need only the seam. It needs only the Subject type and the proxy wiring, not the policy evaluator.

OUT of scope: evaluating groups/users in `allowWhen` and lifting the config guard (W-P1-GPOL-11).

**What to build.** A `gateway.RequestMeta` parameter on `OnRequest` and its callers, fakes and tests.

**Requirements**

- New `gateway.RequestMeta{Subject *identity.Subject}` in `internal/mcp/gateway`. `OnRequest` gains a trailing `meta RequestMeta` parameter: `OnRequest(sessionKey, method, url string, hdr http.Header, body []byte, meta RequestMeta) Verdict`. Change it on the `proxy.MCPGateway` interface (internal/proxy/proxy.go:196), the `proxy.WSScanner` interface (proxy.go:214), the `ws.Pump` gateway interface (internal/mcp/ws/pump.go:32), `gateway.Gateway.OnRequest`, and every fake and caller (including `internal/mcp/stdio` and `cmd/proxy/mcp.go` if they call it).
- `mcpRequestScan` in internal/proxy/http.go passes the request's verified subject (`s.subject` from W-P1-VRFY-02; nil unless status valid), on HTTP/1.1 and on h2 streams (same function).
- `ws.Pump` gets a `Subject *identity.Subject` field set by the proxy at the upgrade from the verified identity of the upgrade request and passes it with every frame (`p.GW.OnRequest(p.SessionKey, "", "", nil, msg, gateway.RequestMeta{Subject: p.Subject})`); the subject is fixed for the connection, so a token expiring later does not change it (documented).
- The stdio pump passes the zero `RequestMeta` (nil subject); documented: group-gated tools are denied over stdio (W-P1-GPOL-11).
- The gateway ignores `meta` in this ticket; all verdicts are unchanged. `internal/identity` is a leaf package, so the import adds no cycle.

2. internal/mcp/gateway: add RequestMeta, change OnRequest.
3. internal/proxy/proxy.go, http.go, ws.go and internal/mcp/ws/pump.go, internal/mcp/stdio: change the interface declarations and callers.
4. Run `go test -race ./internal/mcp/... ./internal/proxy ./cmd/proxy`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

Red first: fails to compile before the parameter exists.
- [ ] Over WebSocket the subject verified on the upgrade request is passed with each frame: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestMCPWS_SubjectFromUpgrade`.
- [ ] The stdio pump passes a nil subject: `go test ./internal/mcp/stdio -run TestStdioPumpNilSubject`.
- [ ] Gateway verdicts are unchanged with and without a subject: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway`.
- [ ] Existing suites pass with the new signature: `go test -race ./internal/mcp/... ./internal/proxy ./cmd/proxy`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 7/14 · W-P1-GPOL-11

**Support groups/users in MCP tool allowWhen conditions**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-11) is the second half of the original MCP ticket #63: it makes `allowWhen` on an MCP tool require a group or user (for example a `pay` tool limited to `finance`), using the subject that W-P1-GPOL-04 plumbed into `OnRequest`. A failure uses the existing Kind `mcp_tool_condition`; a nil subject never satisfies a group or user condition. It lifts the MCP part of the W-P1-GPOL-01 guard, which is safe because W-P1-GPOL-06 already makes old workers deny a scoped tool.

OUT of scope: per-group argument constraints (later phase); task-scope `mcp.scopes` allowWhen (stays rejected); the session key stays `agentID:domain`.

**What to build.** Changes in `internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go` and the config guard.

**Requirements**

- `compiledCondition` gains an `identity.Principals` built in `compileConditions` from `AllowWhen.Groups/Users` (the shared matcher from W-P1-GPOL-02, so MCP and HTTP policy match identically: exact case-sensitive groups, exact `sub`, verified email only).
- `conditionDenies(cc, now, subject)` fails when the condition has groups/users and the match result is `NoIdentity` (Finding Detail `no verified identity`), `NotMember` (Detail `user not permitted`) or `TruncatedMiss` (Detail `groups truncated`; in enforce mode the Verdict.Reason is `identity_groups_truncated` from `internal/denyreason`, never a plain deny). A member found in a truncated list passes. All existing time and agent conditions are unchanged and combine with AND.
- Kind stays `mcp_tool_condition`; enforce mode blocks, monitor mode records the Finding and passes. Group names, emails and user ids never appear in Detail, Findings or metric labels.
- Conditions only narrow: a tool denied by allow/deny lists or scope is never re-permitted by a condition.
- A nil subject (stdio, anonymous, invalid or expired token) is denied for any tool with a group/user condition.
- Remove the MCP tool-level part of the W-P1-GPOL-01 guard in `internal/config`; the denylist and task-scope paths stay rejected. The wire projection (`AllowWhenScoped` and the `!identity-scoped` sentinel, W-P1-GPOL-06) is already in place.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/mcp/gateway (conditions_groups_test.go) and internal/proxy.
2. internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go: extend compiledCondition, compileConditions and conditionDenies.
3. internal/config/mcp.go: lift the MCP tool allowWhen guard.
4. Run `go test -race ./internal/mcp/... ./internal/proxy ./internal/config`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given tools.allow [pay] and constraints.pay.allowWhen{groups:[finance]} in enforce mode, an eng subject is denied with Kind `mcp_tool_condition`, a finance subject passes, and a user listed in `users` passes: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestConditionGroups`. Red first: fails before conditions read the subject.
- [ ] A nil subject is denied with Detail `no verified identity` and a different member with `user not permitted`: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestConditionGroups_NoIdentityAndNonMember`.
- [ ] Truncated groups: a member found in a truncated list passes; a non-member with GroupsTruncated is denied with Verdict.Reason `identity_groups_truncated`: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestConditionGroups_Truncated`.
- [ ] In monitor mode an eng call passes and the Finding is recorded: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestConditionGroups_MonitorMode`.
- [ ] A tool denied by the allow/deny list or scope is not re-permitted by a satisfied condition: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestConditionGroups_OnlyNarrow`.
- [ ] End to end through the proxy, HTTP and WebSocket requests use the request/upgrade subject, and the stdio pump denies a gated tool: `go test ./internal/proxy ./internal/mcp/stdio -run 'TestMCPGroupCondition'`.
- [ ] Groups on an MCP tool allowWhen now load; groups on a denylist entry or a task-scope allowWhen are still rejected: `go test ./internal/config -run 'TestMCPAllowWhenGroupsAccepted|TestGuardStillRejectsOtherPaths'`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-05, GitHub #64) keeps the original key and covers the replay half of the original #64: `policyeval.Evaluate` replays recorded events with the recorded user so `warden policy eval` shows which users a candidate change affects. The other half of #64, the shadow lint `config.LintScoped`, moved to W-P1-GPOL-12 so that it needs only the schema and the dashboard editor (W-P1-GPOL-08) can use it without waiting for replay.

Events without a valid recorded identity replay as anonymous and are counted separately, so pre-identity traffic is not mistaken for user impact. The P2 approvals replay (W-P2-APPR-03) builds on this subject handling.

Replay calls `EvaluateFor(policy.RequestContext{Domain, Port, Scheme, Method, Path, Subject})` with the same method/path derivation as today (the #371 form when both were recorded, destination-only otherwise). `Conditional` and `NoMatch` replay as deny.
- Replay keeps groups/users on the replay policy (`DeepCopy` clones them); `rateLimit` and `timeWindow` are still stripped as today.
- `EvalDiff` gains `AffectedUsers []string` (distinct, the email else the sub, sorted, capped at 20), `AffectedUsersTotal int` and `AnonymousCount int` (disagreeing events without a valid identity); the diff key `(domain, port, method)` is unchanged.

- Output contains only sub or email, never tokens or group lists. Recorded groups are a point-in-time snapshot, stated in the command help.

**Add config.LintScoped shadow warnings and print them in policy eval**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-12) was split from the original #64 "affected users in policy eval" (now W-P1-GPOL-05). A scoped entry is useless when an unscoped or wildcard entry for the same destination already admits everyone; this lint finds that. It needs only the schema (W-P1-GPOL-01), so it can be built in parallel with the evaluator, and the dashboard editor (W-P1-GPOL-08) shows its warnings.

OUT of scope: replay and affected users (W-P1-GPOL-05); the dashboard display (W-P1-GPOL-08).

**Requirements**

Warnings contain entry indexes and domain patterns only, never group or user values. Output order is deterministic.

Red first: fails to compile before the function exists.

### 10/14 · W-P1-GPOL-07

**Report groupPolicy support in the heartbeat and flag old workers**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#245](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/245)

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-07, GitHub #245) is visibility only: workers that do not understand scoped rules deny scoped destinations (W-P1-GPOL-06), and operators need to see which workers those are. It adds one capability value, `grouppolicy/v1`, to the heartbeat `caps` list and flags workers that lack it while the served policy has scoped rules. The heartbeat body struct, the CP-side decode and the registry storage of `caps` are owned by W-P1-BLOCK-10 (worker caps, which also advertises `blocklist/v1`); this ticket only adds the value and the badge.

OUT of scope: the caps struct and its decode/store (W-P1-BLOCK-10); wire fail-closed behaviour (W-P1-GPOL-06).

**What to build.** A capability constant, the worker advertisement, a fleet flag and the CP log.

**Requirements**

- Add `grouppolicy/v1` as a constant next to the other capability values defined by W-P1-BLOCK-10, and append it to the `caps` list in `RemoteProvider.Heartbeat` (internal/config/remote.go). The body stays under the CP's 4096-byte limit.
- Caps bound: the `caps` list is bounded by W-P1-BLOCK-10, which owns and enforces it (at most 16 entries, each at most 32 characters and matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]{0,31}$`). This ticket adds no decode or limit of its own, and `grouppolicy/v1` must satisfy that pattern so it is never dropped by the bound.
- The CP computes `scopedEntries` for the served policy (count of `scopedAllowlist` entries plus MCP tools with a scoped condition) once per ETag. The fleet snapshot (`internal/controlplane/registry.go`) marks a worker `noGroupPolicy` when `scopedEntries > 0` and its stored caps lack `grouppolicy/v1`; legacy heartbeats without `caps` are flagged too.
- The fleet view (internal/dashboard) shows a `no groupPolicy` badge for flagged workers.
- The CP logs once per worker per ETag `msg=worker_lacks_grouppolicy` with `proxy_id` and `scoped_entries`, never group names.
- Heartbeats without `caps` keep working.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/controlplane, internal/config and internal/dashboard.
2. internal/config/remote.go: advertise the capability.
3. internal/controlplane (controlplane.go, registry.go): scopedEntries per ETag, fleet flag, once-per-ETag log.
4. internal/dashboard: badge in the fleet view.
5. Run `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/config ./internal/dashboard`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The worker heartbeat body contains `grouppolicy/v1` in `caps` alongside the other capabilities and stays under 4096 bytes: `go test ./internal/config -run TestHeartbeat_AdvertisesGroupPolicy`. Red first: fails before the value exists.
- [ ] A heartbeat with `{"policyETag":"x","caps":["grouppolicy/v1"]}` is not flagged; a heartbeat with other caps only, and a legacy `{"policyETag":"x"}`, are flagged when scoped rules exist and not flagged when none exist: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestHeartbeat_FlagsWorkersWithoutGroupPolicy`.
- [ ] A heartbeat carrying `grouppolicy/v1` plus 20 other valid caps stores at most 16 caps and the CP still answers normally (the bound is W-P1-BLOCK-10's; this test pins that the new value does not break it): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestHeartbeat_GroupPolicyCapsBounded`.
- [ ] The log line appears once per worker per ETag and contains no group names: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerLacksGroupPolicyLogOnce`.
- [ ] The fleet JSON exposes `noGroupPolicy` and the served dashboard HTML renders the `no groupPolicy` badge from it: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestFleetNoGroupPolicyBadge`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Edit groups/users in the dashboard policy editor**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#246](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/246)

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-08, GitHub #246, relabelled M) lets admins add groups/users to allow entries and MCP `allowWhen` in the CP policy editor and shows which rules are scoped. It covers three surfaces: the editor chips, the policy views' `scoped` badge and the lint warnings from W-P1-GPOL-12, plus the server-side round trip, which is why it is M. The editor saves through the existing dashboard policy write path (`SetPolicyWriter(func(config.Policy) error)` on `/dashboard/api/policy`), so validation and normalization come from the config loader. It depends on the guard having been lifted for allow entries (W-P1-GPOL-10) and MCP conditions (W-P1-GPOL-11).

OUT of scope: any change to enforcement; the worker dashboard stays read-only.

**What to build.** Changes in `internal/dashboard/index.html`, the policy GET/POST handlers and the CP write path tests.

**Requirements**

- `internal/dashboard/index.html`: chip inputs for groups and users per allow entry and per MCP tool allowWhen. Every value is rendered through the existing `esc()` helper or `textContent`, never concatenated raw into HTML.
- Saves use the existing editor method on `/dashboard/api/policy` and `config.AllowlistEntry` / `MCPToolCondition`; the CP validates through the same config loader and returns 400 with the error and leaves the served policy and ETag unchanged on invalid input (empty value, over-long list).
- The policy GET response marks each allow entry and MCP tool `scoped: true` when it has groups/users, so the CP and worker policy views render a `scoped` badge without client-side logic, and includes `lint: [...]` from `config.LintScoped` (W-P1-GPOL-12) which the editor shows next to the entries.
- Saved groups/users come back normalized and sorted so ETags and the policy-history diff stay deterministic.
- The worker dashboard stays read-only and shows the badge and lint only.
- JSON responses never contain a raw `<script>` from a chip value (Go's JSON encoder escapes `<`), and the HTML renders it as text.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing Go tests first in internal/dashboard and internal/controlplane.
2. internal/dashboard: add `scoped` and `lint` to the policy GET response; ensure the POST path passes groups/users through unchanged.
3. internal/dashboard/index.html: chip inputs, badge, lint display using esc().
4. internal/controlplane write path: confirm groups/users round-trip through the policy YAML writer.
5. Run `go test -race ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Saving `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng], users: [Alice@Corp.Example]}` through the CP policy writer returns and re-reads groups [eng] and users [alice@corp.example], and an MCP allowWhen with groups round-trips: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyWrite_ScopedRoundTrip`. Red first: fails while the guard rejects groups.
- [ ] Saving an empty group value returns 400 with the validation error and the served ETag is unchanged: `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard -run TestPolicyEdit_ScopedInvalid`.
- [ ] The policy GET marks scoped entries and tools `scoped: true` and returns the LintScoped warnings: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestPolicyGET_ScopedAndLint`.
- [ ] A group value `<script>alert(1)</script>` saved and read back appears in the GET JSON without a literal `<script>`; the served index.html renders chips through `esc(` or `textContent` and contains no `innerHTML` assignment of an unescaped chip value (static check on `indexHTML`): `go test ./internal/dashboard -run 'TestPolicyGET_EscapesMarkup|TestIndexChipsAreEscaped'`.
- [ ] The worker dashboard handler still rejects policy writes (no writer) and shows the badge: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestWorkerDashboardScopedReadOnly`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-10`](identity-policy.md#514--w-p1-gpol-10) Decide scoped allow entries on every request with the request subject, add reasons and metrics and lift the allow-entry guard; [`W-P1-GPOL-11`](identity-policy.md#714--w-p1-gpol-11) Support groups/users in MCP tool allowWhen conditions; [`W-P1-GPOL-12`](identity-policy.md#914--w-p1-gpol-12) Add config.LintScoped shadow warnings and print them in policy eval

### 12/14 · W-P1-GPOL-09

**Add group policy scenarios on the L1 harness**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#247](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/247)

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-09, GitHub #247, relabelled M) proves the feature's done-when end to end on the in-process L1 harness (`test/harness`, `test/scenarios`), using the in-process OIDC issuer fake and scenario scaffolding of W-P1-VRFY-05. The original #247 held 8 scenarios, a real-Dex run and the docs; it was split into this ticket, the docs ticket W-P1-GPOL-13 and the real-Dex check W-P1-GPOL-14.

OUT of scope: documentation (W-P1-GPOL-13); the real Dex run (W-P1-GPOL-14).

**What to build.** Scenarios in `test/scenarios` registered in `scenarios_list.go`; no new Go package.

**Requirements**

- Scenarios (names are subtest names; each asserts on `h.Events()`, `h.Logs()`, `h.Metrics()` and the fake upstream's `Requests()`): `groups_member_allowed` (valid eng token over Proxy-Authorization and over X-Warden-Identity), `groups_nonmember_denied` (`group_not_allowed`), `groups_anonymous_denied`, `groups_expired_denied` (`identity_required`, event identity_status expired), `groups_keepalive_mixed_users` (eng then sales on one keep-alive tunnel), `groups_h2_per_stream`, `groups_no_ca_conditional` (raw tunnel needs a subject at CONNECT), `groups_raw_bytes_conditional` (non-TLS bytes after a Conditional CONNECT are denied), `groups_truncated` (member in a partial list allowed, non-member `identity_groups_truncated`), `groups_mcp_tool_gated` (finance allowed, eng denied, enforce mode), `groups_old_worker_denies` (the CP wire loaded through a frozen pre-change decoder denies the scoped host and the gated tool) and `groups_policy_eval_affected_users` (replay lists only eng users).
- Every deny scenario asserts the fake judge received zero calls and the upstream received nothing; every allow scenario asserts the upstream never saw Proxy-Authorization or X-Warden-Identity.
- Token minting uses the VRFY-05 issuer fake (valid, expired, wrong-aud tokens and a groups claim, including a truncated one); no real IdP and no network beyond loopback. Scenarios use `h.Eventually` and the fake clock, no sleeps.
- The scenarios work against the CP-served policy (fleet mode) so the scoped projection and merge are exercised.
- Scenario output never prints token strings.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the scenario functions in a new test/scenarios/groups.go and register each with its Opts in scenarios_list.go.
2. Add the small harness helpers needed (a group-claim option on the issuer fake) in test/harness if VRFY-05 lacks them.
3. Run `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/groups_'`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/groups_'` passes all twelve scenarios. Red first: with the stage change of W-P1-GPOL-10 reverted locally the member and mixed-user scenarios fail.
- [ ] No scenario observes `Proxy-Authorization` or `X-Warden-Identity` at the upstream, and the judge fake has zero calls in every deny scenario (asserted inside the scenarios).
- [ ] `groups_old_worker_denies` fails if the wire projection of W-P1-GPOL-06 is removed (proves the fail-closed wire end to end).
- [ ] `go test ./test/scenarios` (the full catalog) still passes. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-10`](identity-policy.md#514--w-p1-gpol-10) Decide scoped allow entries on every request with the request subject, add reasons and metrics and lift the allow-entry guard; [`W-P1-GPOL-11`](identity-policy.md#714--w-p1-gpol-11) Support groups/users in MCP tool allowWhen conditions; [`W-P1-GPOL-05`](identity-policy.md#814--w-p1-gpol-05) Show affected users in policy eval replay

### 13/14 · W-P1-GPOL-13

**Document group-scoped rules**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-13) was split from the original #247 "e2e test and docs" so that the documentation is owned and checkable on its own. It documents the matching rules and the fail-closed cases of the merged feature; every statement is tied to a test that already exists.

OUT of scope: code changes; the scenarios (W-P1-GPOL-09).

**What to build.** New `docs/group-policy.md` plus links and a synced example in `configs/config.example.yaml`.

**Requirements**

- New `docs/group-policy.md` covering: `groups`/`users` on allow entries and MCP `allowWhen`; literal, case-sensitive group matching; users as `sub` or verified email; the denylist stays global; a non-member is denied (never sent to the judge); anonymous, invalid, expired and conflicting identities get `identity_required`; truncated group lists (`identity_groups_truncated` when the group is not found in a truncated list); stdio denies group-gated tools; a Conditional CONNECT without a CA is denied and non-TLS or unknown protocols are denied; h2/gRPC are decided per stream; a scoped raw tunnel is cut at token expiry and is not cut by a policy swap; old workers deny scoped destinations and the fleet view flags them (`grouppolicy/v1`); the `warden policy eval` affected-users output and `--user`; the lint warnings; metrics `warden_policy_scoped_total`; the future P5 `<issuer>:<group>` namespacing note.
- The reasons table in the doc lists `identity_required`, `group_not_allowed` and `identity_groups_truncated` and a Go test checks that they equal the entries in `denyreason.Declared()`.
- `configs/config.example.yaml` has a group-policy example between the marker lines `# --- group-policy example ---` and `# --- end group-policy example ---` written as commented YAML that parses when uncommented.
- Link the new doc from `docs/architecture.md` (policy section) and the README docs list.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing doc tests first in internal/config (or cmd/proxy) docs_test.go.
2. Write docs/group-policy.md; add the example block to configs/config.example.yaml; add the links.
3. Run `go test ./internal/config ./cmd/proxy -run 'GroupPolicyDoc|ExampleConfigGroup'`, `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` and scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The example block in configs/config.example.yaml, uncommented, loads with the real config loader and normalizes: `go test ./internal/config -run TestExampleConfigGroupExample`.

### 14/14 · W-P1-GPOL-14

**Add the real-Dex group policy check on the L2 identity stack**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The group-policy feature (epic #59) is delivered as: W-P1-GPOL-01 schema + guard, W-P1-GPOL-06 fail-closed wire, W-P1-GPOL-02 evaluator, W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum and CONNECT handling, W-P1-GPOL-10 per-request scoped decisions (lifts the allow-entry guard), W-P1-GPOL-04 subject plumbing into the MCP gateway, W-P1-GPOL-11 group/user `allowWhen` (lifts the MCP guard), W-P1-GPOL-05 affected users in `policy eval`, W-P1-GPOL-12 shadow lint, W-P1-GPOL-07 heartbeat capability, W-P1-GPOL-08 dashboard editor, W-P1-GPOL-09 L1 scenarios, W-P1-GPOL-13 docs and W-P1-GPOL-14 the real-Dex check. The L1 scenarios (W-P1-GPOL-09) prove the behaviour against a fake issuer. This ticket (W-P1-GPOL-14) was split from the original #247 and repeats the core cases once against a real Dex token with LDAP groups from the seeded users of W-P1-DEX-02, on the L2 identity stack of W-P1-DEX-04. It needs Docker, so it is gated by the e2e build tag and runs in the CI `e2e` job only.

OUT of scope: everything covered by W-P1-GPOL-09.

**What to build.** One L2 test in `test/e2e`.

**Requirements**

- New `test/e2e/group_policy_test.go` (`//go:build e2e`) with `TestGroupPolicyDex` using the W-P1-DEX-04 stack: a worker with a CA, identity mode attribute and `{domain: <fake upstream host>, groups: [eng]}`; a Dex token for an eng user (fetched with the DEX-02 token script helper) is allowed over Proxy-Authorization and over X-Warden-Identity; a Dex token for a user without the group is denied with `group_not_allowed`; no token is denied with `identity_required`; an MCP tool gated to a group behaves the same.
- Assertions use the event store and the fake upstream; the test never prints tokens; the seeded LDAP users come from the DEX-02 recipe, no external account.
- The test skips with a clear message unless the L2 environment is available.

**Implementation plan**

1. Read test/e2e/shared.go and the W-P1-DEX-04 helpers; write the test.
2. Run `make e2e-scenario NAME=TestGroupPolicyDex` where Docker is available.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `make e2e-scenario NAME=TestGroupPolicyDex` passes in the CI `e2e` job; the eng token is allowed, the non-member denied with `group_not_allowed` and the anonymous request denied with `identity_required`.
- [ ] `go vet -tags e2e ./test/e2e/...` is clean and the file is not compiled without the tag. `scripts/check.sh` passes.
